To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effect of target dose in-homogeneity on BED is significant for SBRT and that it is more pronounced for higher dose per fraction.

a small dose inhomogenity (<5%–10%) in the target significantly reduces the corresponding BED and EUD compared to the case when the target dose is uniform, and that the effect of target dose in-homogeneity on the corresponding BED is more pronounced for SBRT than standard fractionation.

the dose inhomogeneity within the treatment target can significantly affect the biologically effective dose in the planning target, and that the effect is more prominent for hypofractionated treatments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of dose inhomogeneity in the target on BED.
the impact of target dose in homogeneity on the biological effect of radiation in the target.
the effect of dose nonuniformity on BED and E UD in SBRT.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the dose inhomogeneity in the PTV should be minimized as much as possible in SBRT, but it is also important to keep in mind that a relatively small non-uniformity in the dose in the target can have a significant impact on tumor control.
a dose inhomogeneity of <5%–6% is recommended in the target volume for SBRT, and a more stringent requirement of <3%–4% is recommended in case of a dose per fraction of 10 Gy.
dose inhomogeneity in SBRT can have significant effects on BED and EUB and therefore on local control and normal tissue complications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dose non-uniformities in the target should be minimized for SBRT.
a small dose inhomogeneities in the PTV can significantly reduce BED.
a small dose inhomogeneities in the target can significantly reduce the BED and EUD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dose inhomogeneity in the treatment volume can have an important effect on the biological outcome of treatment.
the target dose distribution in the case of SBRT should be carefully evaluated in order to avoid significant reductions in BED and EUD.
dose inhomogeneity should be taken into consideration in the evaluation of BED for SBRT.
